searchText: <@297710785025671168> You can regenerate all state by syncing from block 0, so as long as the chain is available, you can eventually recover all state. You can think of the blockchain as being a highly specialized compression algorithm for current state, it is just very .xpensive to decompress (takes days). Ahh, ok gotcha, thanks! actually, blockchain is larger than the full state 🙂 Hmm, really? I thought the chain itself was smaller than the state? so it would be easier to download a state snapshot (and it will be available if ReGenesis does not happen too often) Maybe I'm thinking of headers only that is smaller? How big is full chain (headers + bodies)? If our representation, state is smaller. https://ledgerwatch.github.io/turbo_geth_release.html#Disk-space Current state (plain): 47 Gb Headers: 7.56 Gb Block bodies: 152 Gb Hmm, I must have been thinking about headers. there could of course be representations where state is larger I wonder if there is some way to incentivize state compression golfing? like if you represent state as a merkle tree in the database, it is probably the same size Where people are incentivized for creating an algorithm that will regenerate state as of a specific block using the fewest bytes (on the wire) possible. well, curious thing about GasToken2 is that all of the GasToken2 contracts can be compressed to a very small piece of data all you need is the address of the GasToken2 factory, number of contracts created, and a bitmap of which ones were self-destructed There are a nearly unbounded set of potential opportunities for compression like that. But the point very quickly comes when it is easier to just download then to compress/uncompress Depends on what your constraints are. If you are bandwidth constrained, but not compute constrained, then an extreme compression algorithm may be preferable. I had that happen to me sometimes. If I needed to transfer 500 Gb file over the WAN, I could try to compress/transfer/decompress, or just transfer. And often just transfer is quicker (my constraint was time) <@!301186049323958275> maybe rather than "compression" your metaphore works better if you treat the chain history as "error coding" (though it still doesn't hold up to close scrutiny) 🤷 Error encoding? bonus data to deal with incidental corruption. ability to reconstruct the original data as long as M/N of the data is still intact (like I said, the metaphore doesn't hold up to close scritiny) it looks like we can soon reduce the size of state representation in turbo-geth to 8Gb 🙂
